hints: First translate the original template CCA TTC ACG GCG TTA GCA into amino acids, then compare each option triplet by triplet to spot exactly which two triplets have changed.
Remember the genetic code is degenerate, so a changed triplet does not always mean a changed amino acid. Check the table to see if TTC to TTG or ACG to ACA still codes for the same amino acid.
walkthrough:
**Translate the original sequence**

Lovely start, let us get our baseline. Use the table to decode each triplet in order.

CCA = glycine, TTC = lysine, ACG = cysteine, GCG = arginine, TTA = asparagine, GCA = arginine. So the original is gly-lys-cys-arg-asparagine-arg.

**Understand what we are looking for**

Each option has two base changes (two mutations). But because some amino acids have more than one triplet, a mutation can be silent.

We need the option where both changed triplets give a genuinely different amino acid, not the same one and not just a silent swap.

**Test each option against the table**

Let us check quickly:

A changes TTC to ATC (lysine to STOP) which is different, but TTA to TTG is still asparagine, so only one change.

B changes ACG to ACA (still cysteine) and GCG to GCA (still arginine), so zero changes.

C changes GCG to CCG (arginine to glycine) which is different, but GCA to GCC is still arginine, so only one change.

D changes TTA to TTC (asparagine to lysine) and GCA to GGA (arginine to proline). That is two real amino acid changes, so D is the answer.

options.A: Only one effective change. TTC to ATC changes lysine to STOP, but TTA to TTG is still asparagine, so it is a silent mutation.
options.B: No amino acid change. ACA is still cysteine like ACG, and GCA is still arginine like GCG, so both mutations are silent.
options.C: Only one effective change. GCG to CCG changes arginine to glycine, but GCA to GCC is still arginine, so it is silent.
options.D: Both mutations change the amino acid. TTA to TTC changes asparagine to lysine, and GCA to GGA changes arginine to proline.
